findings.where: First screen (hero), at both widths: the left column below the supporting paragraph at 1440 px, and the end of the framed hero at 390 px
findings.fault: The page has no way to get in touch with Mark on its first screen. The hero has a name, the nav, the line, a paragraph and the photograph, but no address and no contact panel. parts.txt lists no contact link anywhere on the page. The palette names a pad-yellow 'address strip', but no strip is laid out. On desktop, the place it would naturally go, under the paragraph inside the frame, is empty paper.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has read Mark's line and wants to contact him finds nothing to act on and no address to copy. The founder would object too: the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark, with the address shown, on the first screen they judge first.

findings.where: Below the fold, between the article specimen and the motion sketch: the Download entry 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' with its 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line, at both widths
findings.fault: The lavender motion panel starts right under the last line of the Download entry, with almost no gap (about 2 px at 1440). Every other section break on the page has a wide band of paper. Proximity makes the article's closing download read as the top of the motion panel, and the article ends without a pause.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article specimen can't tell where the article stops. The founder, judging the article page as 'the product', sees its ending run into a different tile part.

findings.where: Below the fold, the motion sketch panel (desktop-05, phone-03/04)
findings.fault: If you squint, the motion panel is the heaviest block below the fold. It is a large saturated box running wider (170–1270 px) than every other section. Its label and content are pushed in (194 px and 450 px) off the left edges the other sections share (170 px and 426 px). The page's loudest shape is the specimen of a 1 s fade, not Mark's article, and it breaks the continuity of the column edges every other section keeps.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading down the tile: the eye lands on a technical sketch instead of the article. The shifted edges make the sheet look assembled rather than set.

findings.where: Palette row: the four swatches (paper, grey, blue, yellow), at both widths
findings.fault: Each swatch has its own shape: a sharp outlined rectangle, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse, and a rectangle with a thick blue border. The similarity lens fails, because swatches in one row should read as one kind of thing. Here the shape differences suggest a meaning (a button? a focus state?) that the labels never explain.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Angélique, reading the palette as the reference for later pages, can't tell whether the ellipse or the blue border is part of how each colour is meant to be used.

findings.where: Motion sketch timing table on the phone (phone-04)
findings.fault: The four-column table is kept at 390 px. The Element column shrinks to about one word wide, so 'Hold: the sheet is already still and readable' runs to five lines and the second row to eleven, while Start and Length sit in empty tall cells. The table reads as a ragged column of single words.
findings.who_objects: Anyone checking the motion sketch on a phone has to piece the descriptions back together word by word.

findings.where: First screen at 1440 px: the 'Placeholder' caption under the portrait
findings.fault: The caption sits outside the hairline frame, pressed into the last few pixels of the screen under the frame's bottom edge. By common region it belongs to nothing: it is cut off from the photograph it describes by the frame line, and it is crammed against the bottom of the viewport.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first, sees a stray line of small text hanging off the bottom edge of an otherwise clean, framed composition.
